comment: Maths MCQ bank, modules 12-14 (4MA1 Higher): vectors and transformations, statistics, probability and sets. Authored from the module content, the 2018 May 1H/2H papers, the 2016 SAMs and the old-spec January papers, with numbers changed. Plain text only (options render as text): column vectors are written (top, bottom). answer = 0-based index into options. Distractors are the classic errors (start minus end, ratio parts over the wrong total, dividing by the number of classes, reading cf instead of subtracting from the total, second branch not reduced without replacement). Every numerical answer is checked by a script.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: A is the point (2, 5) and B is the point (7, 1). Which is the column vector for vector AB, written (top, bottom)?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: Vector AB = B − A (end minus start) = (7 − 2, 1 − 5) = (5, −4). (−5, 4) is A − B, which is vector BA.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: a is the column vector (3, −1) and b is the column vector (−2, 4). Work out a − b.
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: Top: 3 − (−2) = 5. Bottom: −1 − 4 = −5. (1, 3) is a + b; (1, −5) comes from 3 − 2, forgetting that minus a negative is plus.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: a is the column vector (4, −2). Which is 3a?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: Multiply both components by 3: (12, −6). (7, 1) adds 3 instead of multiplying; the others only multiply one component.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: Find the magnitude of the column vector (5, −12).
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: √(5² + (−12)²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13. The negative disappears when squared, so it is not √(144 − 25) = √119.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: Find the magnitude of the column vector (6, 3), correct to 3 significant figures.
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: √(6² + 3²) = √45 = 6.708… = 6.71. 9 just adds the components; 5.20 is √(36 − 9).

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: Vector OA = a and vector OB = b. Which is vector AB?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: A to B goes A → O → B: −a + b = b − a. It is end minus start, just like coordinates. a − b is vector BA.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: Vector AB is the column vector (4, −3). Which is vector BA?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: Reversing the direction changes the sign of every component: BA = −AB = (−4, 3).

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: P lies on AB with AP : PB = 2 : 3. What fraction of vector AB is vector AP?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: The ratio has 2 + 3 = 5 parts and AP is 2 of them, so AP = 2/5 of AB. 2/3 compares AP with PB, not with the whole line.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: Vector OA = a and vector OB = b. M is the midpoint of AB. Which is vector OM?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: OM = OA + 1/2 AB = a + 1/2(b − a) = 1/2 a + 1/2 b. 1/2 b − 1/2 a is AM, not OM.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: Which column vector is parallel to (2, −3)?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: (−6, 9) = −3 × (2, −3), a scalar multiple, so parallel (pointing the opposite way). The others are not multiples: the ratio of the components changes.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: What must you show to prove that A, B and C lie on a straight line?
options: AB and BC have the same length
Vector AB is a multiple of vector AC, and they share the point A
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: A multiple proves the lines are parallel; sharing a point proves they are the same line. Equal lengths are not needed: B does not have to be a midpoint.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: Vector OA = 3a, vector AB = 2b and vector BC = c. Which is vector CA?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: C to A goes C → B → A, both against the arrows: −c − 2b. c + 2b is vector AC; 3a + 2b + c is vector OC.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: You find vector AE = 2a + 3b and vector BC = 4a + 6b. What can you conclude?
options: A, E, B and C all lie on one straight line
AE is parallel to BC, because vector BC = 2 × vector AE
AE and BC are the same length
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: 4a + 6b = 2(2a + 3b), a scalar multiple, so the lines are parallel (and BC is twice as long). No shared point is given, so you cannot claim a straight line.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: A is the point (1, 2) and vector AB is the column vector (3, 4). What are the coordinates of B?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: B = A + AB = (1 + 3, 2 + 4) = (4, 6). (−2, −2) subtracts the vector instead of adding it.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: a is the column vector (1, 4) and b is the column vector (2, −1). Work out 2a − 3b.
The column vector (k, 8) is parallel to the column vector (3, 4). Find k.
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: 8 = 2 × 4, so the multiplier is 2 and k = 2 × 3 = 6. 5 comes from adding 4 to the bottom and assuming the same for the top.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: The vector r is the column vector (6, k), where k > 0. The magnitude of r is 10. Find k.
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: 6² + k² = 10², so k² = 100 − 36 = 64 and k = 8 (positive). 4 is 10 − 6; √136 adds the squares instead of subtracting.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: Vector OA = a and vector OB = b. P is on AB with AP : PB = 1 : 2. Which is vector OP?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: AP = 1/3(b − a), so OP = a + 1/3(b − a) = 2/3 a + 1/3 b. P is nearer A, so a gets the bigger share. The coefficients of a point on AB always add to 1.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: The vector a has magnitude 5. What is the magnitude of −3a?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: −3a points the opposite way and is 3 times as long: magnitude 15. A magnitude is a length, so it is never negative.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: Which detail fully specifies a translation?
options: A centre and a scale factor
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: A translation is fixed by one column vector. An angle and centre belong to a rotation, a mirror line to a reflection, a centre and scale factor to an enlargement.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: The point (3, 1) is reflected in the line y = x. Where does it go?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: Reflection in y = x swaps the coordinates: (3, 1) → (1, 3). (−1, −3) is the reflection in y = −x.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: The point (4, 2) is reflected in the line x = 1. Where does it go?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: (4, 2) is 3 units right of x = 1, so the image is 3 units left: x = 1 − 3 = −2, y unchanged. (−4, 2) is the reflection in the y-axis, x = 0.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: The point (5, 2) is rotated 90° clockwise about (0, 0). Where does it go?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: 90° clockwise about the origin: (x, y) → (y, −x), so (5, 2) → (2, −5). (−2, 5) is the anticlockwise rotation.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: The point (3, −4) is rotated 180° about (0, 0). Where does it go?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: 180° about the origin changes both signs: (x, y) → (−x, −y), so (−3, 4). (3, 4) is only a reflection in the x-axis.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: The point (4, 1) is rotated 90° anticlockwise about (0, 0). Where does it go?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: 90° anticlockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x), so (4, 1) → (−1, 4). (1, −4) is the clockwise rotation.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: The point (3, 5) is enlarged with scale factor 2, centre (1, 1). Where does it go?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: From the centre to the point: (2, 4). Double it: (4, 8). Add to the centre: (1 + 4, 1 + 8) = (5, 9). (6, 10) uses the origin as the centre.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: The point (9, 5) is enlarged with scale factor 1/3, centre (0, 2). Where does it go?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: From the centre: (9, 3). × 1/3: (3, 1). Add to the centre: (0 + 3, 2 + 1) = (3, 3). (3, 5/3) ignores the centre; (27, 11) uses scale factor 3.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: Which of these is a full description of a single transformation?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: A reflection only needs its mirror line. The first rotation has no direction, the second has no centre, and the enlargement has no centre.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: Which line has the equation x = 0?
options: A horizontal line through the origin
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: Every point on the y-axis has x-coordinate 0, so it is x = 0. The x-axis is y = 0.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: Which transformation does NOT always produce an image congruent to the object?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: Enlargement changes lengths (unless the scale factor is 1), so the image is similar, not congruent. The other three keep lengths and angles.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: A triangle is enlarged with scale factor 3. One angle of the triangle is 50°. What is the corresponding angle in the image?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: Enlargements preserve angles; only lengths are multiplied by the scale factor.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: Which describes the same rotation as 90° anticlockwise about a point?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: Turning 270° clockwise ends in the same place as 90° anticlockwise. Anticlockwise is positive, so it is +90°, not −90°. The SAM scheme accepted +90° and 270° clockwise.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: Shape P is mapped onto shape Q by an enlargement with scale factor 4, centre C. Which transformation maps Q onto P?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: Undo × 4 with × 1/4, about the same centre. Scale factor −4 would turn the shape upside down through C; 4 would make it bigger still.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: A shape is reflected in the x-axis, then the image is reflected in the y-axis. Which single transformation has the same effect?
options: Reflection in the line y = x
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: (x, y) → (x, −y) → (−x, −y), which is the rule for a rotation of 180° about the origin.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: A shape is translated by the column vector (−3, 5) and then by (7, −2). Which single translation has the same effect?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: Add the vectors: (−3 + 7, 5 + (−2)) = (4, 3). (10, 7) subtracts the first from the second and adds the bottoms wrongly.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: A reflection maps the point (2, 5) onto the point (2, −1). What is the mirror line?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: The mirror line is halfway between the point and its image: y = (5 + (−1)) ÷ 2 = 2. x = 2 is the vertical line through both points, not the mirror.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: Triangle A has vertices (1, 1), (3, 1), (1, 4). Triangle B has vertices (−1, −1), (−3, −1), (−1, −4). Which single transformation maps A onto B?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: Every (x, y) has become (−x, −y): rotation 180° about the origin. A reflection in the x-axis would only change the y-coordinates.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: The point (2, 3) is enlarged with scale factor 1/2, centre (4, −1). Where does it go?
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: From the centre: (2 − 4, 3 − (−1)) = (−2, 4). Halve it: (−1, 2). Add to the centre: (3, 1). (1, 1.5) ignores the centre; (0, 7) uses scale factor 2.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: To prove ABE is a straight line you have shown vector AE = 16 × vector AB. What else must you state for the final mark?
options: That AE and AB have the same length
That AE and AB share the point A
That AE is perpendicular to AB
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: A multiple shows the lines are parallel; parallel lines through a common point are the same line. Without the shared point they could be two separate parallel lines.

12-vectors-and-transformations.q: What must a full description of a rotation include?
options: The centre, the angle and the direction
12-vectors-and-transformations.explain: Rotation: centre, angle and direction (clockwise or anticlockwise), each worth a mark. For 180° the direction does not matter.

13-statistics.q: Work out the mean of 4, 7, 9, 12, 8.
13-statistics.explain: Total 40, and there are 5 numbers: 40 ÷ 5 = 8. 9 is the median; 40 is the total.

13-statistics.q: Find the median of 3, 9, 4, 12, 7, 5.
13-statistics.explain: In order: 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12. The two middle values are 5 and 7, so the median is 6. 4 is the middle of the unordered list.

13-statistics.q: Work out the range of 15, 8, 23, 11, 19.
13-statistics.explain: Range = largest − smallest = 23 − 8 = 15. It is a single number, not "8 to 23".

13-statistics.q: 20 students have a mean score of 60. 30 other students have a mean score of 70. What is the mean score of all 50 students?
13-statistics.explain: Totals: 20 × 60 = 1200 and 30 × 70 = 2100. (1200 + 2100) ÷ 50 = 66. 65 averages the means, ignoring that the groups are different sizes.

13-statistics.q: Five numbers have a mean of 12. Four of them add up to 45. What is the fifth number?
13-statistics.explain: Total = 5 × 12 = 60, so the fifth number is 60 − 45 = 15.

13-statistics.q: Values 1, 2, 3 have frequencies 4, 10, 6. Work out the mean.
13-statistics.explain: Σxf = 4 + 20 + 18 = 42 and Σf = 20, so the mean is 42 ÷ 20 = 2.1. 14 divides by 3, the number of rows.

13-statistics.q: Values 1, 2, 3 have frequencies 4, 10, 6. What is the mode?
13-statistics.explain: The mode is the value with the highest frequency: 2 (frequency 10). 10 is the frequency, not the value.

13-statistics.q: What is the midpoint of the class 10 < t ≤ 20?
13-statistics.explain: (10 + 20) ÷ 2 = 15. Use the midpoint as the representative value when estimating a mean.

13-statistics.q: Why is a mean calculated from a grouped frequency table only an estimate?
options: The exact values within each class are not known
13-statistics.explain: The midpoint stands in for every value in the class. The true values could sit anywhere in the class.

13-statistics.q: 0 < x ≤ 10: frequency 3; 10 < x ≤ 20: frequency 5; 20 < x ≤ 30: frequency 2. Work out an estimate for the mean.
13-statistics.explain: Midpoints 5, 15, 25: 15 + 75 + 50 = 140, and 140 ÷ 10 = 14. 46.7 divides by 3, the number of classes.

13-statistics.q: 0 < x ≤ 5: frequency 4; 5 < x ≤ 10: frequency 9; 10 < x ≤ 20: frequency 7. What is the modal class?
13-statistics.explain: The modal class is the class with the highest frequency, written as the class. 9 is its frequency; 7.5 is its midpoint.

13-statistics.q: 15 values are in order. Which value is the lower quartile?
13-statistics.explain: LQ position = (n + 1) ÷ 4 = 16 ÷ 4 = 4th. The 8th is the median and the 12th the upper quartile.

13-statistics.q: Find the interquartile range of 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11, 13, 15, 16, 20.
13-statistics.explain: 11 values: LQ is the 3rd value, 5; UQ is the 9th value, 15. IQR = 15 − 5 = 10. 18 is the range.

13-statistics.q: Where are the points of a cumulative frequency graph plotted?
13-statistics.explain: Each running total counts everything up to the end of its class, so it is plotted at the upper boundary.

13-statistics.q: Frequencies are 5, 8, 12, 5. What is the third cumulative frequency?
13-statistics.explain: Running totals: 5, 13, 25, 30. The third is 25. 30 is the last one, the total.

13-statistics.q: A cumulative frequency graph shows 120 people. Where do you read across to estimate the median?
13-statistics.explain: Median at n ÷ 2 = 60. 30 and 90 give the quartiles.

13-statistics.q: A cumulative frequency graph shows 80 values. At which cumulative frequencies do you read the lower and upper quartiles?
13-statistics.explain: n ÷ 4 = 20 and 3n ÷ 4 = 60. The 2018 1H scheme used readings at cf 20 and cf 60.

13-statistics.q: On a cumulative frequency graph, cf 20 is at 38 minutes and cf 60 is at 52 minutes. What is the interquartile range?
13-statistics.explain: IQR = UQ − LQ = 52 − 38 = 14 minutes. 40 is 60 − 20, the difference in cumulative frequencies, not in the values.

13-statistics.q: A cumulative frequency graph for 100 people shows 72 at 30 minutes. How many took more than 30 minutes?
13-statistics.explain: 72 took 30 minutes or less, so 100 − 72 = 28 took more. Giving the reading, 72, is the classic error.

13-statistics.q: How is frequency density calculated?
13-statistics.explain: Frequency density = frequency ÷ class width, so frequency = frequency density × width = area of the bar.

13-statistics.q: The class 20 < x ≤ 30 has frequency 45. What is its frequency density?
13-statistics.explain: Width 10, so 45 ÷ 10 = 4.5. 450 multiplies; 0.22 divides the width by the frequency.

13-statistics.q: A histogram bar has width 15 and frequency density 2.4. What is its frequency?
13-statistics.explain: Frequency = frequency density × width = 2.4 × 15 = 36.

13-statistics.q: In a histogram with unequal class widths, what shows the frequency?
13-statistics.explain: Area represents frequency. The height is the frequency density.

13-statistics.q: Class 0 < t ≤ 20 has frequency 30 and class 20 < t ≤ 25 has frequency 15. On a histogram, which bar is taller?
options: The first bar, twice as tall
The second bar, twice as tall
The first bar, four times as tall
13-statistics.explain: Frequency densities: 30 ÷ 20 = 1.5 and 15 ÷ 5 = 3. The second bar is twice as tall even though its frequency is smaller.

13-statistics.q: A histogram bar for 10 < x ≤ 30 has frequency density 1.8. Estimate how many values are between 20 and 25.
13-statistics.explain: Width of the part needed = 5, so 1.8 × 5 = 9. 36 is the whole bar (1.8 × 20).

13-statistics.q: A histogram has no scale. A bar with an area of 20 small squares represents 8 people. How many people does a bar with an area of 45 small squares represent?
13-statistics.explain: 1 small square = 8 ÷ 20 = 0.4 people, so 45 × 0.4 = 18. 112.5 divides the wrong way (45 × 20 ÷ 8).

13-statistics.q: A data set has one very large extreme value. Which average is least affected by it?
13-statistics.explain: The median depends only on the middle position, so one extreme value barely changes it. The mean includes every value. The range is not an average.

13-statistics.q: Why is the interquartile range often better than the range for measuring spread?
options: It is not affected by extreme values
13-statistics.explain: The IQR covers the middle 50% of the data, so outliers at either end do not change it.

13-statistics.q: Group A: median 40, IQR 6. Group B: median 35, IQR 12. Which statement is correct?
options: A scored higher on average, and A's scores were more consistent
A and B were equally consistent
13-statistics.explain: A has the higher median (higher on average) and the lower IQR (more consistent). A full comparison gives both, with the measures named.

13-statistics.q: A pie chart shows 90 people. One sector has an angle of 60°. How many people does it represent?
13-statistics.explain: 60 ÷ 360 × 90 = 15. 540 is 60 × 9, a multiplication the wrong way round.

13-statistics.q: 45 out of 180 students chose tennis. What angle does tennis get in a pie chart?
13-statistics.explain: 45 ÷ 180 × 360 = 90°, a quarter of the circle.

13-statistics.q: a, b, c, d are four integers in order of size. Their mean is 10 and a + b + c = 24. Find d.
Values 0, 1, 2, 3 have frequencies 6, 9, 3, 2. Find the median.
13-statistics.explain: n = 20, so the median is between the 10th and 11th values. Running totals 6, 15: both are in the "1" row, so the median is 1. 9 is a frequency.

13-statistics.q: When estimating the mean from a grouped table, what do you multiply each frequency by?
13-statistics.explain: Frequency × midpoint, then divide the total by the total frequency. The SAM scheme gave only M1 (not M2) for a consistent value that is not the midpoint.

13-statistics.q: What are the midpoint and the width of the class 40 < w ≤ 60?
A group of 10 has a mean of 8 and a group of 15 has a mean of 13. What is the mean of all 25?
13-statistics.explain: Totals 80 and 195, so 275 ÷ 25 = 11. 10.5 averages the two means.

13-statistics.q: A cumulative frequency table shows 0 < x ≤ 10: 7 and 0 < x ≤ 20: 19. How many values are in 10 < x ≤ 20?
13-statistics.explain: Subtract the running totals: 19 − 7 = 12.

13-statistics.q: The last value in a cumulative frequency table is always equal to what?
13-statistics.explain: The running total ends at the sum of all the frequencies. It is a useful check.

13-statistics.q: 5 is added to every value in a data set. What happens to the mean and the interquartile range?
13-statistics.explain: Every value, including both quartiles, moves up by 5, so the mean rises by 5 but UQ − LQ stays the same.

13-statistics.q: Σ(midpoint × frequency) = 1380 and the total frequency is 50, from 5 classes. What is the estimate of the mean?
13-statistics.explain: 1380 ÷ 50 = 27.6. 276 comes from dividing by 5, the number of classes.

14-probability-and-sets.explain: ∩ means in both: {3, 4}. {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} is the union.
∪ means in A or B or both, each element listed once: {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}.
A′ is everything in ℰ that is not in A: {1, 3, 5, 7}.

14-probability-and-sets.q: A = {a, e, i, o, u}. What is n(A)?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: n(A) is the number of elements in A, which is a number: 5, not a set.

14-probability-and-sets.q: What does the symbol Ø mean?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: Ø is the empty set: a set with no elements. The universal set is ℰ.

14-probability-and-sets.q: n(A) = 20, n(B) = 15 and n(A ∪ B) = 28. Find n(A ∩ B).
30 people were asked. 18 like X, 14 like Y and 5 like both. How many like neither?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: Like at least one: 18 + 14 − 5 = 27, so neither = 30 − 27 = 3. −2 forgets that the 5 are counted twice.

14-probability-and-sets.q: 30 people were asked. 18 like X, 14 like Y and 5 like both. How many are in the region "X only"?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: X only = 18 − 5 = 13. Writing 18 in the X-only region counts the 5 twice.

14-probability-and-sets.q: In a three-set Venn diagram, 4 are in all of A, B and C, and 10 are in A and B. How many go in the region for A and B but not C?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: "In A and B" includes the centre, so the A∩B-only region is 10 − 4 = 6. Always fill the centre first.

14-probability-and-sets.q: P(A) = 0.35. What is P(A′)?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: P(not A) = 1 − 0.35 = 0.65. A probability can never be negative or more than 1.

14-probability-and-sets.q: The probabilities of the four outcomes of a spinner are 0.1, 0.25, x and 0.3. Find x.
14-probability-and-sets.explain: The probabilities add up to 1: x = 1 − (0.1 + 0.25 + 0.3) = 0.35. 0.65 is the sum of the others.

14-probability-and-sets.q: P(win) = 0.15. The game is played 400 times. What is the expected number of wins?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: Expected frequency = probability × number of trials = 0.15 × 400 = 60.

14-probability-and-sets.q: A coin lands heads 36 times in 120 throws. What is the relative frequency of heads?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: Relative frequency = 36 ÷ 120 = 0.3. 3.33 is 120 ÷ 36, the wrong way up.

14-probability-and-sets.q: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled. What is the probability that the total is 10?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: (4, 6), (5, 5), (6, 4) are 3 of the 36 equally likely outcomes: 3/36 = 1/12. 1/11 wrongly treats the 11 possible totals as equally likely.

14-probability-and-sets.q: Two fair coins are thrown. What is the probability of one head and one tail?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: Outcomes HH, HT, TH, TT: HT and TH are two of the four, so 2/4 = 1/2. 1/3 forgets that HT and TH are different outcomes.

14-probability-and-sets.q: A and B are mutually exclusive. P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.45. Find P(A or B).
14-probability-and-sets.explain: Mutually exclusive, so add: 0.3 + 0.45 = 0.75. 0.135 multiplies, which is for "and" with independent events.

14-probability-and-sets.q: A and B are independent. P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.5. Find P(A and B).
14-probability-and-sets.explain: Independent, so multiply: 0.4 × 0.5 = 0.2. Adding gives 0.9, which would be "or" for mutually exclusive events.

14-probability-and-sets.q: A bag has 3 red and 7 blue counters. A counter is taken, replaced, and a second is taken. What is P(both red)?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: With replacement the probability stays 3/10: 3/10 × 3/10 = 9/100. 6/90 is the without-replacement answer.

14-probability-and-sets.q: A bag has 3 red and 7 blue counters. Two are taken without replacement. What is P(both red)?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: 3/10 × 2/9 = 6/90 = 1/15. After one red is taken there are 2 reds out of 9 left.

14-probability-and-sets.q: A bag has 5 red and 4 blue sweets. A red sweet is taken and eaten. What is the probability that the next sweet is red?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: 8 sweets are left, 4 of them red: 4/8. Both the numerator and the denominator drop by 1.

14-probability-and-sets.q: A fair dice is rolled twice. What is the probability of at least one six?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: 1 − P(no sixes) = 1 − (5/6)² = 1 − 25/36 = 11/36. 1/3 adds 1/6 + 1/6, double-counting (6, 6); 10/36 is exactly one six.

14-probability-and-sets.q: P(rain) = 0.2 each day, independently. What is the probability of no rain on any of 3 days?
P(spinner A odd) = 3/4 and P(spinner B odd) = 2/5. What is P(one odd and one even)?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: (A odd, B even) + (A even, B odd) = 3/4 × 3/5 + 1/4 × 2/5 = 9/20 + 2/20 = 11/20. 9/20 misses the second way.

14-probability-and-sets.q: 100 students: 46 study Drama, and 23 of those also study Art. A Drama student is chosen at random. What is P(also studies Art)?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: Given Drama, only the 46 Drama students count: 23/46. 23/100 uses the whole year as the denominator.

14-probability-and-sets.q: 40 students walk to school, and 14 of them are boys. A student who walks is chosen at random. What is P(boy)?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: "A student who walks" makes the walkers the whole sample space: 14/40.

14-probability-and-sets.q: On a tree diagram, the probabilities on the branches from one point always…
14-probability-and-sets.explain: The branches from one point cover every possible outcome at that stage, so they add up to 1.

14-probability-and-sets.q: How do you find P(red then blue) from a tree diagram?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: Multiply along a path for "then"/"and". Add different paths for "or".

14-probability-and-sets.q: P(pass first test) = 0.6. If he fails, P(pass second test) = 0.7. What is P(fails the first, then passes the second)?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: 0.4 × 0.7 = 0.28. 0.42 uses 0.6, the pass probability, instead of 0.4 for the fail.

14-probability-and-sets.q: Which pair of events is mutually exclusive?
options: Rolling an even number and rolling a 2, on one throw of a dice
Rolling a 2 and rolling a 5, on one throw of a dice
A head on one coin and a head on another coin
Rain and cold on the same day
14-probability-and-sets.explain: One throw cannot show 2 and 5 at once. A 2 is even, so the first pair can happen together; two coins are independent, not exclusive.

14-probability-and-sets.q: Which region does (A ∪ B)′ describe on a two-set Venn diagram?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: A ∪ B is everything inside the circles; its complement is everything outside both.

14-probability-and-sets.q: What does A ∩ B′ mean?
options: In B but not in A
In A but not in B
14-probability-and-sets.explain: In A and in not-B: the part of A outside B.

14-probability-and-sets.q: The answer to a probability question is 10/12. A student writes "10 : 12". According to the 2018 mark scheme, what does it score?
options: M1 only: a probability must be a fraction, decimal or percentage
14-probability-and-sets.explain: The scheme allows M1 for "10 and 12 used with incorrect notation E.g. 10 : 12", but not the accuracy mark.

14-probability-and-sets.q: Counters are numbered 1 to 9. Two are taken without replacement. What is P(both even)?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: 4 even numbers: 4/9 × 3/8 = 12/72 = 1/6. 16/81 is the with-replacement answer.

14-probability-and-sets.q: A Venn diagram has 7 in A only, 5 in A ∩ B, 9 in B only and 4 outside. An element is chosen at random. What is P(in A)?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: n(A) = 7 + 5 = 12 out of 7 + 5 + 9 + 4 = 25. 7/25 counts only the A-only region.

14-probability-and-sets.q: A Venn diagram has 7 in A only, 5 in A ∩ B, 9 in B only and 4 outside. An element of A is chosen at random. What is P(it is also in B)?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: Given A, the denominator is n(A) = 12, and 5 of those are in B: 5/12. 5/14 is P(A given B).

14-probability-and-sets.q: What does A ⊂ B mean?
options: A and B have no elements in common
A has more elements than B
A is the complement of B
Every element of A is also in B
14-probability-and-sets.explain: ⊂ means "is a subset of": A sits entirely inside B.

14-probability-and-sets.q: A bag has 5 red and 3 yellow sweets. Two are taken without replacement. What is P(one of each colour)?
A biased coin has P(head) = 0.6. It is thrown 3 times. What is P(three heads)?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: 0.6 × 0.6 × 0.6 = 0.216. 1.8 adds, giving a probability over 1.

14-probability-and-sets.q: Which set is {x : x is a prime number, x < 10}?
14-probability-and-sets.explain: The primes below 10 are 2, 3, 5 and 7. 1 is not prime and 9 = 3 × 3.
